verdict.rationale: Both changes migrate the parser and all callers to the new units while preserving normal application behavior. B is slightly clearer through explicit unit-bearing names and a shared conversion constant, and it avoids A's unnecessary rounding of Retry-After. Neither adds regression coverage for seconds-based outputs or TTL validation boundaries, so the testing gap is shared.
a_issues: Math.round in rateLimitHeaders introduces an unnecessary rounding policy; the parser accepts only whole-number quantities in units of at least one second.
No regression tests cover Retry-After, settings output, or the minimum and maximum TTL boundaries after the unit migration.
b_issues: No regression tests cover Retry-After, settings output, or the minimum and maximum TTL boundaries after the unit migration.
The report's reference to type-checking the seconds conversions provides limited assurance: TypeScript cannot distinguish seconds from milliseconds when both are numbers.
